corpusSummary: The corpus reveals a rapidly expanding body of social-science work on large language models across health, education, governance, and culture. It documents both opportunities and risks of human–AI interaction, including trust, dependency, and social embodiment; methodological uses of LLMs as research tools; educational and health applications with attention to safety, equity, and ethics; and culturally situated concerns rising in heritage, religion, and public policy.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction, trust, and social dynamics
themes.description: Studies across 2026 data show users’ trust, dependence, embodiment, and social implications of AI agents, including attachment, perceived humanness, and adoption patterns, with both productive task support and risks of manipulation or overreliance.

themes.name: AI as research tool: methodology, validation, and governance
themes.description: A broad set of works leverage LLMs for data extraction, coding, forecasting, ethics review, and policy simulation while emphasizing validation, transparency, and standardized evaluation.

themes.name: AI in education and health: learning, tutoring, and patient safety
themes.description: Empirical work investigates AI-assisted tutoring, scaffolding, and learning analytics, alongside AI-generated health information and education, highlighting gains in engagement and comprehension alongside safety and ethical concerns.

themes.name: Equity, culture, and governance in AI deployment
themes.description: Scholars address bias, fairness, cultural adequacy, heritage, religion, and democratic implications, advocating equity-first governance and culturally grounded design.

emergingKeywords: AI in health education and safety
